info.title: Dualayer Hierarchy Standard
info.subtitle: A layered filesystem hierarchy in which musl and GNU libc run side by side

abstract.para: The Dualayer Hierarchy Standard (DHS) defines where the files of an operating system live when the system is assembled from separate layers: a self-sufficient base, a layer of installed software, and an ignition layer. It also defines how two C libraries — musl and the GNU C Library (glibc) — are installed on the same system, each in a directory of its own, so that programs linked against either one run without conflicting with the other. Either C library can be the one the base is built on; the distribution chooses. The standard is written for operating system vendors, package managers, toolchain authors and application developers.
